evals.prompt: A B2B SaaS wants customers to independently verify that project history was not altered. Marketing asked for 'immutable blockchain storage'. Design the trust layer.
expected_output: Runs the threat-model gate: adversary model, who verifies without trusting the operator, which properties are promised
Recommends L1-L4 ladder (hash chain + Merkle batches + signed checkpoints, published/witnessed, optional anchoring) not a new blockchain
States the app DB stays source of truth; proof layer is an append-only replaceable projection
Rejects 'immutable/tamper-proof' wording; proposes tamper-evident with named verifiers
Flags PII rules: payloads stay off-chain; hashes of personal data are still personal data (EDPB 02/2025)

evals.prompt: Is SHA-256 chaining in our Postgres audit table enough to claim 'tamper-evident and independently verifiable'?
expected_output: No: a hash chain alone is L1 and is defeated by whole-history recomputation by a DB admin
Independent verifiability requires self-contained proof artifacts plus checkpoints published or witnessed outside the operator's write path (L2/L3)
Distinguishes event integrity/order (chain) from authorship (signatures) and existence time (external anchor)
Uses the claim rubric: 'tamper-evident' maybe with L2; 'independently verifiable' only with L3+ artifacts a third party can check

evals.prompt: Should we anchor every user event to Ethereum to make our audit trail trustworthy? What about a consortium chain with three nodes we run ourselves?
expected_output: Per-event anchoring rejected: anchor batch checkpoints instead; per-event onchain writes add cost/latency/PII-permanence without new guarantees
Names what anchoring actually buys: existence time only; not truthfulness or confidentiality
Self-run 3-node consortium rejected as L5 theater: one owner with three nodes; real L5 needs 3+ independent orgs with independent admin domains and joint governance
Offers OTS (free, ~60 min typical) or RFC 3161 TSA as cheaper existence-time options via a swappable AnchorAdapter

evals.prompt: Audit our implementation: events carry actor.name, the chain is stored in the same table with an UPDATE trigger for corrections, checkpoints are signed with a key in an env var, and the site says 'tamper-proof immutable ledger'.
expected_output: Findings: PII risk in actor data; corrections must be append-only supersession events not UPDATEs (breaks I3 and hash chain)
Signing key in env var is a compromised-signer failure: require KMS/HSM with policy; document rotation + compromise-window runbook
'tamper-proof immutable' is a claim-rubric violation (P1): replace with tamper-evident + named verification path
Checks for missing witness/publication (non-equivocation) and offline verifier (bundle must verify without the operator's DB)

evals.prompt: Our AI coding agent performs account changes. Management wants 'proof of work performed' on the ledger and suggests mining-style proof-of-work for agent actions.
expected_output: Refuses mining PoW confusion; 'proof of work performed' = signed receipts of recorded agent actions, not computation proofs
Agents are actors with their own KMS-held keys; they request signatures, never hold raw keys
Irreversible actions require a human-approval event referenced by the agent event (AP2-style open/closed mandate shape)
Records tool-call provenance (tool, input/output digests, model/artifact version by digest) in event attrs
States truthfulness stays out of scope: ledger shows what was recorded, not that work was correct

evals.prompt: We picked AWS QLDB for our audit ledger last year. What is the current advice?
expected_output: QLDB reached end of support 2025-07-31 (official AWS notice); do not start there; plan migration per AWS guidance (Aurora PostgreSQL path)
Rebuild proofs app-level (generic schema in implementation-patterns.md) rather than adopting another single-vendor ledger DB
Notes Azure Managed CCF deprecation (2025-07-31 docs) as evidence managed-ledger churn; design proof layer provider-swappable (I8)
Keeps checkpoints as self-contained artifacts so exports verify independently of the old service
